resume_test:
I ran these on the five smallest configurations: A-ALARM, DF2-K2-R1, A-CUT, A-PROGRESS and X-READY-ALL (215 parts). Every test used at most 4 Node processes and 1.5 GB of heap. The results are in tmp/model-test.

(1) Reference: I ran run-all.mjs itself, limited to 3 workers of 500 MB by the test-only preload limit-run-all.mjs. It gave 215 parts and 16,977,874 states.

(2) Uninterrupted: run-resumable.mjs on the same configurations (r-full) gave 16,977,874 states and 49,221,400 transitions, exit 0.

(3) Interrupted (r-kill2, with the final code): I killed my own runner with taskkill /F after 111 parts. Its 3 children had exited 7 s later, ended by the watchdog thread. The restart printed "111 final from earlier runs (111 complete)" and ran only the other 104 parts, exit 0. An earlier kill test with code from before the final edits (r-kill: 124 parts done, then 91 after the restart) gave the same outcome.

compare.mjs found 0 differences per part between r-full and r-kill2: states, transitions, status, and every property's verdict and shortest-trace length. Every configuration's totals and verdicts were EQUAL to run-all.mjs's. For example: DF2-K2-R1 3,659,461 / 10,660,653; A-CUT 6,171,304 / 18,011,453; A-ALARM 413,666 / 831,242.

Further checks:
- A torn result file, a leftover temp file and a wrong fingerprint were detected; exactly those 2 parts reran, with 0 differences afterwards.
- With --mem-mb 70 --big-mem-mb 75, 7 parts stayed BOUNDED (exit 1). The next start did not rerun them. --big-mem-mb 300 then ran only those 7, alone, and the total came back to 3,659,461.
- The 14 big parts overlapped no other part in time, and they ran before the next configuration started.
- A second runner on the same folder was refused (exit 2).
- A floor that cannot be met made the runner wait without starting anything.

limits: check.mjs keeps record offsets in a Uint32Array. Past about 93 M states at 2 fields (45-46 bytes per record), or about 83 M at 3 fields (51 bytes), its state store goes silently wrong. run-resumable.mjs reports any such part as a FAILED run ('unsound'), never as complete. At B=8000 the search stops for memory first, at about 50 M states; raising B above about 10,000 can cross that line. Finishing group 11 and parts of groups 9-10 needs check.mjs changed (64-bit offsets or a store on disk) or a bigger machine; I did not change check.mjs.

configs.mjs defines K4 as at most one fault of each kind, because a 15-minute run could not hold more; that is the shrinking the owner's rule forbids. configs-full.mjs adds K4F (k=4 with the K2/K3 caps), which contains every K4 part. K4 stays in the matrix because it is cheaper and its results arrive first; --exclude '*-K4-*' drops it.

Big parts run alone, one at a time. The tail of groups 7-11 is therefore mostly single-core time. Estimated wall time: about 4 h for groups 1-5 (every configuration that is complete-able today at 2 fields, plus 3 fields with 2 faults), about 2-2.5 days for groups 1-9, and about 2.5-3 weeks for the whole matrix. Group 11 ends mostly BOUNDED. estimated_minutes is the midpoint of the whole matrix (about 21 days); the estimate is only good to within a factor of about 2.

No complete run exists yet with the current model for A-FENCE-CE at 2 or more faults, for K4F, for 3 fields with 3 or 4 faults, or for any D configuration other than D2-K2-R1. Those estimates are scaled from DF measurements: 3 fields is about 6.3 x 2 fields; cost is about 10-14 microseconds of one core per state.

run-all.mjs runs as soon as it is imported, so run-resumable.mjs cannot import it. Instead it reads run-all.mjs's source and evaluates its own maximalMultisets, partArg and weight. It refuses to start if that code changes shape, and it checks that the parts cover every fault multiset. In the tests, run-all.mjs was limited to 3 workers and 500 MB by a test-only preload (tmp/model-test/limit-run-all.mjs), because by default it would start 22 workers.

Admission counts each worker as its size plus 150 MB, plus the headroom that running workers may still grow into, measured as working set from tasklist samples every 5 s. The 150 MB is the measured overhead (52-134 MB over 26 parts). I could not measure how far a worker at 8000 MB goes over within the 3 GB test limit; the 4 GB floor is the margin for that.

A result is reused only when its fingerprint matches: hashes of model.mjs and check.mjs, the configuration id, the part, and the resolved parameters. Any edit to model.mjs or check.mjs (another agent is reading the model now) makes every part run again, by design.
A part already BOUNDED at a size of B or more is reported again but not rerun, unless --rerun-bounded or a larger --big-mem-mb is given. A failed run (a crash) is always run again.
